exposure: Embarrassment from breastfeeding in public places
outcome: Barriers to breastfeeding in the first year of life
cohort: The study included a purposive sample of 120 mothers who had infants from birth to 12 months old and were free from mental or physical diseases, attending an immunization outpatient clinic.
finding: The most common barriers to breastfeeding were pain, sore nipples, breast engorgement, perceived insufficient milk supply, public embarrassment, and premature infants.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as one of the most common barriers to breastfeeding related to mothers.
cross-section timing: Infants from birth to 12 months old
gest_age: Premature infants were mentioned as a barrier to breastfeeding, implying gestational age was considered as a factor, but specific gestational age criteria for inclusion/exclusion were not mentioned.
